alignments.note: Interrogative he takes the fronted Do (rule 17); the ASV rewrites it at the head of the second, juxtaposed question, so both Do's belong to the one particle's discontinuous unit (rule 25's distributed interrogative). Competing reading: second Do as the verb's own under rule 17's first limit.
Bare noun construed adverbially; the supplied in belongs to the noun under rule 33. Margin (Is the righteousness ye should speak dumb?) read and set aside.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17); the fronted Do is the particle's.
Adverbial accusative rendered by the adverb uprightly.
Verb with subject pronoun; the second Do placed on the particle.
Vocative takes supplied O ye (rule 36); the ye stands before the noun, not after the imperative-like verb. Margin (O ye gods / mighty ones; judge uprightly the sons of men) read and set aside.

review_notes: Both Do's assigned to the single interrogative particle under rule 25; alternative noted.
